newsitem.title: USA: Weld quitting to avoid delays in Massachusetts.
newsitem.headline: Weld quitting to avoid delays in Massachusetts.

text.p: Massachusetts Gov. William Weld said on Monday he was resigning because he did not want the "people's business here to be held hostage to the fights which are going to occur in Washington."

President Bill Clinton formally nominated Weld last week to be U.S. ambassador to Mexico, but the Massachusetts governor faces stiff opposition from fellow Republican Sen. Jesse Helms. The North Carolina conservative, who chairs the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, has publicly said he objects to the liberal Weld's views on the medicinal use of marijuana and to his drug prosecution record.
Helms has said he will not hold the hearings necessary for confirming Weld's appointment.

"I'm going down there (to Washington). I've got a very straightforward case to make. You know, it's the American way: fairness, due process. If you've got an objection on narcotics policy, let's have a hearing. That's what congressional hearings do," Weld told reporters on his way into the state house.
Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott backed away on Sunday from leading a charge to rescue Weld's troubled nomination.

"Two weeks ago, we might could have worked out something with the chairman," the Missouri Republican said on the NBC programme "Meet the Press," adding, "But the biggest problem right now is Governor Weld shot his foot off (in comments about Helms)."
Earlier this month, Weld called a news conference to challenge Clinton to fight for the nomination and said his differences with Helms reflected an ideological rift in the Republican Party.
"In plain language, I am not Senator Helms' kind of Republican," Weld said then.

Responding on Monday to Lott's remarks, Weld said: "My aim is to try to change the rules a little bit in Washington. Obviously, the existing setup down there is not calculated to have open hearings and open debate. It's kind of analogous to the divided Republican Party."
Weld is to hold a formal news conference announcing his resignation at 5 p.m. EDT (2100 GMT) on Monday.
Lieutenant Governor Paul Cellucci will assume the governorship and thus have an edge for what is expected to be a bruising 1998 race for the office.
